key.ruled: Andrew-direct 2026-09-13 ~03:2xZ card 1, verbatim; the five segments and their order are the ruling
key.container: {bucket} -- the bucket that holds the key; NEVER a segment of the key
key.leaf: {object} -- the file under {partition}; not part of the ruled string
key.source: a registry VENDOR key (a feed) or, for derived tiers, a PRODUCT or SYSTEM key
key.scope_rule: a vendor MASTER keeps its own scope (doctrine R3: two masters of one firm are two scopes, never commingled -- schwab/08242234/, never schwab/49financial/). For every other key the scope is its AUDIENCE: a FIRM when the data is one firm's; global when every firm shares it. A PRODUCT key is a scope only beneath a VENDOR source (a feed for the product: pathfinder/etfs), never beneath itself as the source -- mdpf/global/..., never mdpf/mdpf/... (SC1, v1.5; the master case written at v1.6)
key.table_case: snake_case; a NEW platinum leaf is a kebab-case .json file (the served names); see legacy_served_path
key.legacy_served_path: below {source}/{scope}/platinum/, a LEGACY served path keeps its bytes -- the table, a bare entity-id segment in the partition slot, and the file name -- because the frozen portal requests it by path; the kebab-case and hive forms bind NEW served families only (LGIC_NAMING v1.3, rows S6 and S8). MEMBERSHIP is data, never a name's shape: a path is legacy only if legacy_served_paths lists it (LGIC_NAMING v1.4, row S10)

key.code: tier code is a pipeline's code home (R16), beside its data: {source}/{scope}/code/{built_tier}/{file} -- the table slot carries the tier the code builds (bronze, silver or gold) and the file or bundle is a named leaf; Lambda deployment artifacts take the same form (R16 does not reach them; R1 grades their key). Legacy root code/ homes stay until their pipelines move (LGIC_NAMING v1.3, row S7; the canon's carve-out narrowed as LGIC_CANON-S1). A legacy root code/ key grades OUT-OF-PATTERN, its canonical_form the code-tier key; a verdict is not a mandate to move, so MDPF_CANON's frozen rollback objects keep that verdict and stay (LGIC_NAMING v1.4, row S10)
partition: {entity}={id} -- an entity partition; {entity} is the KEY COLUMN's name as the table carries it (advisor_id=A123), as date is the column in date=YYYY-MM-DD; the file is the object under it (doctrine R2; P1, v1.5)

template_detection.purpose: EN-m-39, LGIC_ENFORCE round 8 (TO LGIC_ENFORCE.TO-EN-m-39-r8): the mechanism distinguishing an S3 KEY TEMPLATE (a producer's key FORMAT STRING) from an S3 KEY (a graded name). A ROW-LEVEL predicate over this key.grammar's own domain, never a TYPE-level exclusion -- R-62 refused moving S3Key into types_not_graded_by_kind because S3Key is EVERY key, while the 15 rows LABEL_TRUTH_R7.json identifies (key_template_rows) are 15 TEMPLATES.
template_detection.rule: a row's own `current` value, AS OBSERVED before any grade or canonicalization runs, is a KEY TEMPLATE when it carries a brace-delimited token {token} that is NOT one of grade.placeholder's four sanctioned tokens ({system}, {source}, {scope}, {cadence}). Those four are the ONLY tokens a grade itself may OPEN in a canonical_form (grade.placeholder); they are inserted BY THE GRADE and never present in an observed `current` before grading runs -- an actual key carries no brace at all. A brace a row carries BEFORE any grade ran is therefore never a grade-opened placeholder: it is the producer's own runtime substitution field, already present in the repo or live plane's own declaration of the row.
template_detection.test: extract every {[^{}]+} brace-delimited token from the row's raw, pre-grade `current` string; subtract the four sanctioned tokens ({system}, {source}, {scope}, {cadence}); a NON-EMPTY remainder marks the row a KEY TEMPLATE. An EMPTY remainder (no brace at all, the ordinary case for an observed key) leaves the row graded normally under key.grammar.
template_detection.disposition_on_match: ROW_IS_NOT_A_NAME (R-62 (c)): the row is CARDED, not graded, and S3Key is NOT moved in types_not_graded_by_kind -- this is a ROW predicate, never a type exclusion. Every other S3Key row stays inside key.grammar's domain.
template_detection.disposition_on_no_match: an ordinary key: graded under key.grammar exactly as before this field existed; nothing here changes its verdict.
template_detection.measured_against: LGIC_ENFORCE round 7's key_template_rows (LABEL_TRUTH_R7.json, cell EN-t-34): 15 of 15 carry a non-empty remainder (producer_runtime_fields {snap}, {dim_name}, {firm}, {d}, {dc}). The negative arm was run against 91 ordinary S3Key rows drawn from PLACEHOLDER_CAMPAIGN_R6.json (its 106 S3Key rows less the 15 template currents) and returned a non-empty remainder on ZERO of the 91 (LGIC_ENFORCE round 8, EN-m-39, deliverables/0.9.0_WK_LGIC_ENFORCE~3/TEMPLATE_VS_KEY_R8.json).
template_detection.instrument: the same subtraction shape as LABEL_TRUTH_R7.json's own `unsanctioned_brace` re-identification instrument (round 7: brace tokens MINUS the four grade.placeholder sanctions; a non-empty remainder is an unsanctioned brace; 15 of 15 re-identified there independently of round 6's label). This field promotes that instrument from a one-off census script into schema DATA, so a later census reads a RULE rather than re-deriving one.
template_detection.ruled: R-62 (c); LGIC_ENFORCE round 8, cell EN-m-39 (TO LGIC_ENFORCE.TO-EN-m-39-r8, v1.11).
template_detection.scope: WIDENED at v1.12 (LGIC_ENFORCE round 9, cell EN-s-41, TO LGIC_ENFORCE.TO-EN-s-41-r9; the evidence for row LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S17, record deliverables/0.9.0_WK_LGIC_ENFORCE~2/PERCENT_STYLE_SCOPE_R9.json). The object this field detects is the producer's RUNTIME SUBSTITUTION FIELD -- `rule` above already names it so -- and the brace is one SYNTAX of it, never its definition. A row is a KEY TEMPLATE when its raw, pre-grade `current` carries EITHER (a) a brace token as `test` states, OR (b) a python %-style field matching `percent_field_regex`, searched after every '%%' pair is removed scanning left to right. NOTHING ELSE marks a row: `percent_field_excludes` is part of this rule, not commentary on it. PRECEDENCE: `test` and `disposition_on_no_match` above were written brace-only at v1.11 and are left byte-identical as EN-m-39's record; from v1.12 an EMPTY brace remainder leaves a row an ORDINARY key only when (b) ALSO finds no field, and an instrument implementing this field implements `test` AND `percent_field_regex`, never `test` alone. NO GRADE MOVES AT v1.12: no code reads this field (neither lib/opal_naming.py nor .tools/naming-gate.py consults it), and re-grading the rows (b) newly selects -- measured 2 of the 3254 NAMING_CENSUS_REPORT.r8.md rows, both 'silver/%s/' (SILVER_PREFIX_FMT in the bd-49f and bd-cot freshness probes) -- is a LATER round's cut, seated deliberately.
template_detection.percent_field_syntax: exactly four forms: %s ; %d when the next character is NOT a hex digit ; %(name)s or %(name)d ; %0Nd with N in 1-99 (a zero-padded integer; its URL reading, %0N, is a control byte no key or URL carries). Measured at v1.12: selects 2 of 2 census %-rows and 44 of 44 tier-prefixed %-literals in tracked .py source.
template_detection.percent_field_excludes: NOT a field, so NOT a template by (b), each measured ORDINARY in PERCENT_STYLE_SCOPE_R9.json: a literal percent ('%%', a trailing '100%'); a URL-encoded byte, '%' plus two hex digits ('%2F', '%20', '%3A', '%dc' -- which is why %d is refused before a hex digit); every other printf form (%5s, %f, %x, %r, %i); strftime directives other than %d (%Y, %m, %H, %M, %S -- a strftime string is caught only through a %d it carries); the EMPTY brace '{}' (str.format positional, which {[^{}]+} cannot match); an unbraced shell reference $NAME. Admitting any of these is a schema edit with its own population census, never a regex change in an instrument.

bucket.legacy_platform_rule: a PLATFORM bucket that predates platform_bucket's form and that a legacy_addresses.json READ row must name. Legal ONLY as a legacy_addresses.json row's bucket: never a tier home, a scope bucket, a remediation surface or a name for a new bucket. A bucket leaves this list when its last legacy row retires (R19).

resource.scope_when_shared: OMITTED -- a shared resource carries no scope token, never a placeholder
resource.function: names what the resource does. Where the item DESCRIBES the action with a verb, the function is that verb in its base form (publish, fetch, read, build, download); an agent noun describing the resource ITSELF is written as its verb (publisher -> publish, exporter -> export, scanner -> scan), because the kind names the thing. Where the item NAMES the process or subject as a noun phrase (the SmartX platform export, the Orion ingest, the price-refresh queue, pipeline alerts, delivery status), the function is that phrase as named, kebab-case, ONE token (as silver-chain), LESS every token already written in the system or scope slot: Inflection's Orion ingest is orion-inf-ingest, never orion-inf-orion-ingest; a subtraction that leaves no function token RAISES (grade.unplaceable) (FN1b, v1.7). The resource's OWN kind (kind.by_type for its type) is never written in its function; another type's kind that names the subject the resource serves is part of that phrase and stays (mdpf-gold-lambda-role is the role the gold lambda assumes) (FN1c, v1.7). FN1b and FN1c are ONE subtraction, never two ordered steps: remove from the function, in one pass, every token written in the system or scope slot AND every token that is the resource's own kind; if that leaves no function token, the grade RAISES (grade.unplaceable) whichever rule removed the last token, so the result never depends on an order (a LAMBDA mdpf-lambda-lambda RAISES; so does a LAMBDA whose system is orion and whose function is [orion, lambda]) (FN1d, v1.8). FN1b and FN1c bind the GRADE as well as the namer, because both are read from the name alone; the word-choice clauses before them bind the NAMER, who has the item's description, and a grade keeps a function's words as written (FN1, v1.5; v1.7)
resource.qualifier: optional narrowing, written after the function: the TIER (bronze, silver, gold, platinum) or the named TABLE the action acts on, when the item names one -- any other object (figures, files, data, session data) is not written (FN2); a leg; or an environment (dev | prod). A CW_ALARM's qualifier is its condition noun (failure, error, latency), always written (FN3, v1.5)
resource.fifo: an SQS_QUEUE that is FIFO ends in the AWS-required suffix .fifo, written after its kind (queue or dlq): {system}-{scope}-{function}[-{qualifier}]-{kind}.fifo. The suffix is not a token and is never written as a qualifier; name(..., fifo=True) writes it and refuses it on any other kind, and grade() strips it before the grammar (N5) (v1.14)

kind.closed_at_l4: By subtraction from the live plane's 33 node types: ECS_TASK_DEFINITION, STATE_MACHINE, LOAD_BALANCER and ECS_CLUSTER had no kind in the brief's list -- added as task, sfn, lb and cluster (the last two each have one live node, opal-gateway and opal-globgrph, and are resources this estate mints). secret was DROPPED: secrets keep their own slash-path grammar, where a kind suffix would repeat the type. The brief's measured suffixes trigger, publisher, scanner are FUNCTION tokens, not kinds; their canonical spellings are the verbs trigger, publish and scan (FN1, v1.5).

types_not_graded_by_kind.EVENT_RULE: resource grammar with a CADENCE as the last slot (resource.last_slot)
types_not_graded_by_kind.SCHEDULE: resource grammar with a CADENCE as the last slot (resource.last_slot)
types_not_graded_by_kind.LOG_GROUP: derived: /aws/{service}/{resource-name}; conforms when its resource does (log_group)
types_not_graded_by_kind.S3_BUCKET_POLICY: carries its bucket's name exactly (15 of 15 live nodes); graded as that bucket
types_not_graded_by_kind.IAM_USER: NOT GRADED: named by its holder or issuer -- a person, the account root, an external identity provider named by its issuer URL (4 live nodes). The one machine user among them (github-actions-portal) is recorded, not graded; a remediation that converts it to a role takes the role grammar A MACHINE user minted for an Opal box (NFRA_CTLPLN C-IDENTITY, v1.13) is named by the resource grammar with kind user (cloudops-dell1-agent-user); a person, the root and an issuer-named provider stay ungraded.
types_not_graded_by_kind.ROUTE53_RECORD: NOT GRADED: a DNS record name (not_covered)
types_not_graded_by_kind.API_ROUTE: NOT GRADED: a served route contract (not_covered; infra/logic/07_ROUTING_REDERIVATION.md)
types_not_graded_by_kind.EVENT_SOURCE: NOT GRADED: an event-source expression or service name, a different grammar (not_covered)

cadence.daily_definition: daily = fires at most once per calendar day, on five or more days of the week. A weekday restriction (MON-FRI, TUE-SAT, MON-SAT) is a CALENDAR, not a cadence, and is never named: the calendar lives in the schedule's expression and in lib/trading_calendar.py. Once a day on two to four days of the week matches no value and stays undecided (P1, v1.16)

interval_form.rule: a rule that fires on a FIXED interval shorter than a day takes {N}min for N minutes, N from 1 to 59, or {N}h for N hours, N from 2 to 23. 60 minutes is hourly and 24 hours is daily, never 60min, 1h or 24h. The two interval entries in `values` (5min, 1min) are instances of this rule and stay listed because lib/opal_naming.py reads `values`; a reader of cadences accepts `values` OR a token matching `token_regex` (P2, v1.16)
interval_form.not_covered: an interval of a day or more that is not 24 hours or 7 days (rate(72 hours)); several listed hours a day; an Nth-weekday rule; an expression that is not a literal. Each stays undecided and is listed with its reason

cadence.event_rule: a rule with an event pattern and no schedule expression takes {function}-on-{event}: the function is what the rule starts, the event is what it waits for, and the token is decided per rule by reading its target and its pattern. The function is NEVER empty: two rules waiting on one event would share a name (P3, v1.16)

secret.purpose: the credential's kind (credentials, token, key, password, certificate), preceded by the interface it opens when the item names one: api-credentials (FN4, v1.5)

iam_policy.purpose_slot: function -- FN1 and FN2 apply, written as one compound token (read-gold) (FN4, v1.5)

firm_forms_source: A firm's forms (its key and its one sanctioned short form) are the identity registry's rows, infra/logic/registry/scopes.json, and every reader reads them there; this file carries no copy, so one change to the registry moves every name and every fence pattern at once (RULING ONE, v1.9). demo reads as a firm in every naming slot (RULING DM, v1.7); its TENANCY is the registry's DEMO-TENANT class (RULING DEMO, v1.9; Andrew ~01:3xZ 09-13 card 8, R20 X6).
tf_type_map_note: Terraform resource type -> the node_type the grade takes, and the attribute that carries the resource's own name (null: the type carries none). Data, not a grader's private reading (C-S11, W3-S1, v1.9; seeded from LGIC_ENFORCE EN-t-1's census map).
tf_unmapped_own_name_note: Terraform types that carry their own name but map to no node_type: a grade of one RAISES at G1.1 until a node_type is added here (v1.9).

refused_tokens.bd: refused in EVERY slot (Andrew ~03:5xZ card 2). The vendor is blackdiamond; the firm is 49financial. Which of the two a given name means is decided by alias_adjacency (v1.10).
refused_tokens.mockadv: an alias only, recorded in the registry's alias rows as history; never minted

bd.reads_as: VENDOR blackdiamond when a firm token (a registry firm key or its sanctioned short form) is ADJACENT to it, before or after; FIRM 49financial otherwise
bd.test: ADJACENCY to a firm token, never position in the name

examples.cot-bd-session-trigger-lambda-role: vendor -- cot is adjacent, bd sits second
examples.bd-49f-runner-role: vendor -- the case that split two blind judges (LGIC_CANON-W7-S2); canonical blackdiamond-49f-runner-role, verdict ALIAS
examples.bd-allocations: firm -- no firm token adjacent; canonical spells 49financial's form for the slot

bd.either_way: bd is an ALIAS in every slot (refused_tokens.bd); the canonical form spells blackdiamond or the firm's form for the slot
bd.source: GRADING_RULE.md R3 (LGIC_NAMING round 4, coverage N of N); rows LGIC_NAMING-W4-S1, LGIC_CANON-W7-S2; A-3 (v1.10)

system.vendor_as_system_only_when: the resource IS the vendor integration
system.vendor_through_tiers: a resource that builds a firm's data from ONE vendor's feed IS that vendor's integration at every tier it builds (blackdiamond-cot-build-silver-profile); a resource that combines feeds takes the PRODUCT or PLATFORM_SUBSYSTEM that owns the combination (SY1, v1.5). A worked example here is kept outside every naming-exercise item set, so a briefing that carries this file never spells an item's answer (RULING EX1, row S15, v1.7)

reserved.opal: account-level platform resources only; never a null prefix before a real system

grade.signature: (name, type) -> (verdict, canonical_form); type is a node_type value (node_type_vocabulary)
grade.NO-SYSTEM-ASKED: no system is asked of this kind of name (a name led by a refused purpose word such as an AWS service name, a single-token PascalCase inline policy name, a Lambda layer, where no later token and no registry row resolves a system -- Andrew 2026-09-21, ruling 3 / CALL 3; C-VERDICT, LGIC_BLANKFIX BF-t-2): no remedy is owed, and canonical_form carries no {system} placeholder
grade.ALIAS: the grammar holds but a slot carries a registry alias spelling (for example inflection or bd in a resource name's scope slot); canonical_form is printed
grade.OUT-OF-PATTERN: the grammar fails (order, separator, case, a missing or unknown kind, a firm in the system slot); canonical_form is printed
grade.not_graded: a type marked NOT GRADED in types_not_graded_by_kind returns no verdict and is outside the grade's domain -- it is excluded, not a fifth verdict
grade.placeholder: a canonical_form may carry {system}, {source}, {scope} or {cadence} ONLY for a slot the name does not carry. Each is a typed gap, never a guess, filled from its source: {system} from the identity registry's resource-to-system rows (LGIC_ENFORCE), {source}/{scope} from the bucket, {cadence} from the schedule. The verdict stays exact, and the signature stays (name, type). FWD-5's correct name is complete for a name only when no placeholder remains (PH1, v1.5)
grade.unplaceable: RAISES. A name the tokeniser cannot place, a node_type absent from this file, or a token no registry row resolves, is a defect in the tokeniser, this file or the registry and is fixed there -- it is never filed under one of the four verdicts, and there is no fifth

not_covered: Terraform resource labels and module names (the executable layer's authoring surface; measured before its flagger is specified)
AWS-issued identifiers (KMS key ids, CloudFront distribution ids, service principals, VPC endpoint ids)
API route grammar (a served contract; infra/logic/07_ROUTING_REDERIVATION.md)

aws_fixed.rule: names AWS fixes are OUTSIDE the grade's domain, like the NOT GRADED types: excluded, never a fourth verdict. Extended when a new AWS-fixed name is measured (AW1, v1.5)
aws_fixed.by_arn: an IAM_POLICY whose ARN's account field is aws (arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/...) is AWS-managed -- read from the node's ARN, never from the name (ReadOnlyAccess carries no prefix)
aws_fixed.measured: row LGIC_NAMING-W1-S4 over LIVE_NAMES.json (vintage 2026-09-14 12:13:53 UTC): SECURITY_GROUP 1 of 26; IAM_POLICY 9 of 417 by prefix, plus ReadOnlyAccess; LOG_GROUP 4 of 264

renames_authorized: NONE. This schema grades; it moves no live name. Each remediation is minted where the resource lives, cites a row of the tension ranking, and carries its own sign-off.
